title: Electrical power & energy
examples: How do I calculate the power in a light bulb?
What is the difference between power and energy?
If I use a heater for two hours, how much energy did I use?

explain.say: Today we are learning about electrical power and energy.

items: Power measures the rate of energy use.
Energy is the total work done electrically.

explain.say: First we look at power using voltage and current.
Next we see power using current and resistance.
The total energy used is power multiplied by time.
For a kettle, the power is the rate it uses energy.
A common mistake is mixing up power and energy units.

faq.q: What is the unit for electrical power?
faq.a: The standard unit for electrical power is the watt, symbol W. You might also hear it called kilowatts.
asks: What unit do I use for power?

faq.q: How do I find the energy used if I know the power and time?
faq.a: You multiply the power by the time elapsed. The result will give you the energy in joules.
asks: If I have P and t, what is E?
What is the formula for energy from power?

faq.q: Does the formula P = V I always work?
faq.a: Yes, for simple circuits, power equals voltage times current. This is a fundamental relationship.
asks: Can I use V and I to find P?
What is the relationship between V, I, and P?

faq.q: What does the 'R' stand for in the power formulas?
faq.a: R stands for resistance, which is a measure of how much a circuit opposes current flow. It is measured in ohms.
asks: What is R in P = I²R?
What does resistance mean in electricity?

faq.q: If I use a bulb for a long time, is the energy used more or less?
faq.a: The longer you use it, the more total energy you consume. Energy depends on the time duration.
asks: How does time relate to energy consumption?

facts: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred or used.
The relationship P = V I is used to calculate power.
Energy (E) is calculated by multiplying power (P) by time (t).
The unit for energy is the joule (J).

quiz.say: A device uses 12 volts and 2 amperes of current. What is its power?
quiz.why: Power is calculated by multiplying voltage by current, so 12 times 2 equals 24 watts.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the voltage and current together instead of multiplying them.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you cannot simply combine the units like that; the result must be in watts.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the formula requires multiplication, not division, for this calculation.

quiz.say: If a heater has a power of 1000 watts and runs for 5 seconds, how much energy is used?
quiz.why: Energy is power multiplied by time, so 1000 watts times 5 seconds equals 5000 joules.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you forgot to multiply by the time duration of the heater.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you divided the power by the time instead of multiplying.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you added the values together, which is not the correct physical relationship.

quiz.say: A light bulb has a resistance of 4 ohms and draws a current of 3 amperes. What is its power?
quiz.why: We use the formula P equals current squared times resistance: 3 squared is 9, and 9 times 4 equals 36 watts. Wait, 3 squared is 9, and 9 times 4 is 36 watts.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the current and resistance together.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the question asks for power, which is measured in watts, not ohms.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you calculated V times I instead of using the resistance formula.
